boundaries: `saveActiveLayerFrame`'s and `saveAllLayerFrames`' shared layer-kind guard (app.js:4663 and 4699, identical field list: `symbolId||montageId||isNullLayer||isEffectLayer||isGuideLayer||isWidgetLayer||lfsGroup||(duplicator&&!_dupEditSource)||_rigPoseLive||(SMPathFx.hasAny)`) is MISSING `isEffectorLayer`, even though getEffectiveStrokes' own equivalent early-return (app.js:2973, C21k, cited by line only: `if(ld.isNullLayer||ld.isEffectLayer||ld.isGuideLayer||ld.isWidgetLayer||ld.isEffectorLayer)return[];`) treats `isEffectorLayer` IDENTICALLY to the four sibling flags that ARE checked here — the same asymmetry class C21l already documented for `badComponentSourceReason` (app.js:3212-3221), now confirmed independently in a THIRD location. Consequence: if an effector layer's live Paper layer ever holds a stray Path/Raster child (it shouldn't, by convention, but nothing in this scope enforces that), a save here would persist it into `ld.frames[i].strokes` even though getEffectiveStrokes will always render `[]` for that same layer — a write with no possible read. Not fixed here (census scope only); flagged for the next behavioral pass.

Neither guard tests `ld.locked` at all, despite CLAUDE.md's own consumer-list framing naming "locked" as a layer-kind gate alongside `isWidgetLayer`/`symbolId`/`montageId`/duplicator host. A manually-locked-but-otherwise-ordinary layer (locked via the eye/lock UI, unrelated to being a component instance) is saved completely normally by both writers — `locked` only ever blocks live EDITING elsewhere (editRefusalReason, tools.js, cited by name only, out of scope), never saving of whatever content already exists. The `locked:true` stamps this file's own C21l scope applies to component instances (app.js:3302/3433) are redundant with, not a substitute for, the `symbolId` gate already present here — an instance layer is skipped because of `ld.symbolId`, not because of `ld.locked`.

`_smGeomDirty` is READ but never WRITTEN anywhere in this scope: `_canReuseMaterialized` (app.js:4718) reads `lyr._smGeomDirty` as one of its three guard conditions, but the flag itself is set to `true` only by engine-bridge.js's own `_changed` hook (engine-bridge.js:328, cited by line only, CLAUDE.md §5quater) and cleared to `false` only by loadFrame's own per-layer materialize step (app.js:4796) and a second materialize helper (app.js:4999-5005) — both next-slice C21p territory. The issue's own side-effect list groups "_smGeomDirty clear" alongside `_sceneVersion++`/symbolUnionBounds invalidation as if all three were save-writer side effects; corrected here by direct read: neither `saveActiveLayerFrame` nor `saveAllLayerFrames` ever assigns to `_smGeomDirty` or `_matStrokes` — that pairing belongs entirely to loadFrame, the READER of what these two functions write, not to the writers themselves.

`saveAllLayerFrames` (app.js:4693-4710) never increments `window._sceneVersion` — confirmed by an exhaustive grep of every `_sceneVersion` occurrence inside 4373-4728: exactly two, the module-level `=0` declaration (line 4499) and the single `++` inside `saveActiveLayerFrame` (line 4635). This is consistent with the packet-1 lead-in comment (4374-4384), which names only "saveActiveLayerFrame/loadFrame" as the two checkpoints bracketing engine-bridge.js's tick() diffing target — but it means a call path that mutates frame content ONLY via `saveAllLayerFrames` (the 30s autosave interval, most bulk operations, goToFrame's per-OTHER-layer save) does not itself signal tick() that anything changed. Every `saveAllLayerFrames` call site actually read in `source_consumers`/`reconciliation` pairs it with either a `pushUndo`/`pushUndoLayers` call (which does NOT bump `_sceneVersion` either, per its own body at tweens.js:4896, cited by line only) or a sibling explicit `window._sceneVersion++`/`=(...)+1` at the same call site (e.g. timeline.js:2000, tools.js:8436) — so in every OBSERVED case the signal comes from elsewhere in the same call chain, but nothing in `saveAllLayerFrames` itself guarantees that; not verified exhaustively for every one of its ~27 calling files (out of this census's own read-only scope).

`strokesEqual`/`_deepCloseEqual`/`_numClose`/`_normStrokeForCompare` have NO external callers anywhere in the codebase — confirmed by a whole-`src` recursive grep. `strokesEqual`'s SOLE caller in the entire codebase is `_maybePromoteInterpolated` (app.js:4598, same scope); `_deepCloseEqual`'s only callers are itself (recursion, 4401/4420) and `strokesEqual` (4496); `_normStrokeForCompare`'s only caller is `strokesEqual` (4496); `_numClose`'s only caller is `_deepCloseEqual` (4398). This corrects the issue's own prompt text ("every caller of strokesEqual/_deepCloseEqual, expect engine-bridge tick, app.js"): engine-bridge.js's tick() diffing (engine-bridge.js:3947/3960/4234/4237/4325/4352) is driven entirely by comparing `window._sceneVersion`, a completely separate and much cheaper mechanism, and never calls either comparison function. The two comment blocks that open this scope (4374-4384 for `_sceneVersion`/tick, 4385-4394 for `_numClose`/`_deepCloseEqual`/`strokesEqual`) describe TWO UNRELATED "cheap change signal" purposes for two unrelated consumers (engine-bridge.js's tick() vs. `_maybePromoteInterpolated`'s own narrower "was this specific tween frame hand-edited" question), not one shared mechanism.

Two unrelated features share the literal `data.ghostFrame` tag. timeline.js's `selectGhostAll`/`clearGhostSelection` (timeline.js:3799-3846) inserts REAL, editable proxy Paths into `userLayers[activeLayerIdx].children` — the array this scope's own `_writeBackGhostProxies` (4511-4525) and `_collectLayerStrokes` (4563-4576) both iterate — and is the only producer/consumer pair this scope's own code actually interacts with. tweens.js's `renderGhostAll` (tweens.js:4538-4568) is an UNRELATED, read-only onion-style ghost display for OTHER keyframes of the active layer, reusing the identical `data.ghostFrame=fi` tag name (tweens.js:4568) but inserting its items into a dedicated, non-user overlay Paper layer (`ghostAllLayer`, confirmed by direct read: `ghostAllLayer.removeChildren()`/`desP(sd,ghostAllLayer,op)` throughout its own body) — never into any `userLayers[]` entry. Because both this scope's own functions iterate `userLayers[li].children` specifically, `renderGhostAll`'s own tagged items are structurally unreachable from either one, regardless of the shared tag name; a reader who assumed one tag implies one feature would be wrong here.

`_collectLayerStrokes`'s per-child filter (app.js:4574) tests exactly two conditions before accepting a child — `c.data.ghostFrame!==undefined` (skip, real Ghost-All proxy) and, ONLY when `ld.nativeVideo` is set, `!(c.data&&c.data.isMask)` (skip anything that isn't the layer's own mask) — and otherwise accepts any `c instanceof Path` with `segments.length>0` or any `c instanceof Raster`. Cross-checked against every CLAUDE.md §1 tag this scope's own issue text names as needing verification: `isDuplicatorCopy`/`dupIndex` is NEVER tested here because the exclusion happens one level up, at the LAYER, not the child — the duplicator HOST layer is fully skipped by both save writers' own `(ld.duplicator&&!ld._dupEditSource)` gate (app.js:4663/4699) before `_collectLayerStrokes` is ever called on it, and every `isDuplicatorCopy`-tagged stroke dict found in this scope's own grep (app.js:864/867/1774) belongs to `getEffectiveStrokesRendered`'s own synthetic N-way expansion (out of scope, cited by name only), not to any child this loop would ever see. `isBrushTextureCopy` and `isLinkedFillCompanion` are likewise NEVER tested here — confirmed by grep to be legitimate ordinary persisted content (brush dabs and linked-fill companion ribbons are real, independently drawn `Path` children with real segments) that this collector correctly does NOT special-case; they flow through the generic `Path`→`serP()` branch untouched, consistent with CLAUDE.md §1's own note that dabs are excluded from TWEEN MATCHING (tweens.js's `splitTweenables`) but never from persistence itself. `__osLayer`/`__osFrame` (the onion-skin tag pair, tweens.js:4588's `osTagFrame`) never appear as candidates at all: their only two producers, engine-bridge.js's own onion rendering (engine-bridge.js:2636's `onionLayerItems`, cited by line only) and `osTagFrame` itself, both operate on transient scene-graph/overlay items outside `userLayers[]`, confirmed by grep (only engine-bridge.js and tweens.js reference either tag anywhere in src).

`_collectLayerStrokes` is not a pure reader. `enforceChannelStrip(ld,c)` (app.js:5034, next-slice territory, cited by name/line only) is called on every qualifying `Path` child (line 4574) BEFORE `serP(c)` — for a channel-split layer (`ld.channel==='stroke'` or `'fill'`), this MUTATES the LIVE Paper.js item's `fillColor`/`strokeColor` to `null` in place, enforcing the Stroke/Fill/Shadow split going forward (per its own comment at app.js:5025-5033, cited by line only). A save of a channel-split layer therefore has an observable canvas side effect beyond the intended `ld.frames[i].strokes` write — not a bug (the function's own header names this as deliberate, "ON GOING FORWARD, not just at the one-time conversion moment"), but worth recording precisely since every other packet in this scope is otherwise read-then-write over `.data`/stored fields only, never a live-geometry mutation mid-collect.

`_flattenCompoundChildren`'s CompoundPath rescue (app.js:4526-4562) is explicitly framed as a "LAST-DITCH defence" by its own comment (line 4533): every known CompoundPath-producing call site already routes through `insertBooleanResult` (tools.js:6967) per convention, so this function exists purely to catch a hypothetical FUTURE producer that doesn't. It runs unconditionally at the very start of every `_collectLayerStrokes` call (line 4565), for both save writers, on EVERY layer that reaches the collector — not gated on whether that layer's content actually changed since the last save, and not gated on whether the layer even has a CompoundPath child (the `kids.forEach`/`instanceof CompoundPath` check inside is the only gate, line 4553).
